Primary Source Analysis Worksheet Generator

Describe or paste in a primary source and build a printable OPTIC or SOAPSTone worksheet, plus a matching answer key built from your own notes.

Worksheet name

Lets you save more than one worksheet (e.g. one per source you analyze).

Source setup

A sentence or two is enough — this is what students see printed above the questions. Since this is a static site, there's no image upload; describe it in words (an optional image link is below).

One word per line, with an optional definition after a colon: austerity: extreme plainness. Prints as a glossary box under the source.

If the image is hosted somewhere online, paste its link and it will appear on the worksheet. Leave blank to rely on the description only.

Embeds the file directly in this worksheet's saved data — no hosting needed. Takes priority over the Image URL above if both are set.

Large photos are automatically resized (long edge capped at 1600px) before they're saved, to keep this worksheet from eating too much of the browser's storage.

Reading support (optional)

Off by default — when unchecked, the worksheet prints exactly as it does without this section. Turning it on adds a teacher-typed summary and/or a plain-language paraphrase of the source text. Pairs well with “Number each line” above, so students can point back to the exact line in the original wording.

A sentence or two giving the gist before students tackle the full source. Prints as a highlighted box near the top of the worksheet.

Your own plain-language rewrite of the source text. Prints in its own box right under the original.

Framework

Number of blank lines printed under each step's questions on the student worksheet.

Teacher notes / model answers

Fill these in once per step. They stay hidden on the student worksheet and only appear when you print the answer key.

Live preview of exactly what prints.

Runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
